state.misconception_label: Confuses rest and movement on a distance time graph

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I have: This graph shows how far Fido the dog is from his home. What might the negative-sloping section represent? ![A graph with time (secs) on the horizontal axis and distance (m) on the vertical axis. The graph starts at the origin, travels in a straight line up and right, travels horizontally, then travels in a straight line down and right back to the x-axis. ](). I got Fido has fallen asleep because I'm not sure I worked it out the right way.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text:
Let's think about this. From similar cases:
  1. Topic: Read values off a displacement-time graph. Correct answer (D): \( 7500 \mathrm{~m} \). Student selected: \( 0 \mathrm{~km} \). Underlying misconception: Thinks a horizontal line on a distance time graph means a distance of 0. Intervention focus: surface why the selected answer is wrong and walk through the reasoning that leads to the correct answer.
  2. Topic: Calculate the distance travelled using a speed-time graph. Correct answer (C): \( 24 m \). Student selected: \( 30 m \). Underlying misconception: Believes that when finding area under graph you can use the upper y value rather than average of upper and lower. Intervention focus: surface why the selected answer is wrong and walk through the reasoning that leads to the correct answer.
  3. Topic: Read values off a speed-time graph. Correct answer (A): \( 1 \mathrm{sec} \). Student selected: \( 4 \) secs. Underlying misconception: When reading value from graph, reads from the wrong axes.. Intervention focus: surface why the selected answer is wrong and walk through the reasoning that leads to the correct answer.

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Oh right, so a horizontal line doesn't mean zero distance... but I'm still confused about what it actually means then. And for the downward sloping bit, does that mean Fido is getting closer to home, or is he moving backwards or something?
